feature: Picking a clip while a video plays
summary: Clicking a clip, clicking away, and cutting or trimming the picked clip while the 6 minute edit plays now each finish within one frame (16 ms), and the panel names the clip the moment you click it. Closing a window gives its pictures' memory back again.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Timings are from the speed walk on the 6 minute reference edit, worst of three runs.

try.do: Open a screen recording, press Escape so nothing is picked, and press Space to play it.
While it plays, click the clip on V1. Properties and the clip's name come up at the top of the panel at once.
Press Space to stop. The rest of the clip's sections come in under the name, which does not move.
Press Space again, then Escape while it plays. The sections leave from the bottom up.
Click the clip while it plays, then move the pointer over the panel. Every section comes in and it plays on.
Open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below, play it, and click clips, press B and undo. Watch whether the picture stutters.

evaluate: Does the name at the top of the panel tell you soon enough that your click landed?
When you let a clip go while it plays, do the sections leaving one by one read as quick rather than fussy?
Do any picks, cuts or undos while it plays make the picture hesitate?
rough: While it plays, the Properties header shows without its question mark and three dots; they come with the section when play stops or the pointer comes in.
Tool bar and menus follow a pick made during play about a tenth of a second behind the panel's name line.
No mock covers how the panel behaves during playback.
